target_customer: Fashion brands and retailers, plus models who license their likeness for virtual photoshoots
problem: Fashion design and marketing photography are slow and wasteful. The company offered digital garment versions before production and photoreal imagery of clothing on many body sizes.
business_model: B2B SaaS creative suite for fashion brands (AI design and imagery tools); 2024 Persona product paid models per use of their image
product_category: Generative AI creative tools for fashion

founders.name: Daniel Citron
founders.background_notes: YC page describes him as an award winning filmmaker and creative technologist with Harvard listed among affiliations; his Harvard role is not stated. The YC page later lists him as a former founder.

founders.name: John Chirikjian
founders.background_notes: YC page says AI.Fashion was formerly Backlot and that he now works on Starpilot.

technical_complexity.rationale: Physically accurate cloth simulation and photoreal garment imagery were hard but available as research and open tools in 2020; the company began as Backlot, a different product, per the YC page.

defensibility.rationale: No data or network effect is described in the sources; the 2024 Persona product relied on model licensing but was launched years after the batch.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source describes an incumbent response. The 2024 coverage names no competitors.

market_need_then: The YC description cites fashion waste and returns driven by poor fit information. No dated demand data was found in the sources opened.

branding.domain_note: Uses the ai.fashion domain, a new TLD name; the YC page says the company was formerly called Backlot. No purchase details found.

identity.logo: not described in any source found

brand_strength.rationale: Only trade press on the 2024 round and Persona launch was found. The name describes the category rather than distinguishing the company, and no brand pages or community evidence surfaced.

pivots.to: AI.Fashion, an AI creative suite for fashion
pivots.why: Not stated by a source I opened; the YC page only notes the former name.

outcome_analysis: AI.Fashion raised a reported 3.6 million dollar seed round led by Neo in February 2024 and launched the Persona product, then the YC directory marked it inactive with the CEO listed as a former founder and the CTO working on Starpilot. The cause of the wind down is not public, so no failure factors are recorded.
notes: Company website returned HTTP 503 so it could not be read. The seed round is reported by FashionUnited, Pulse 2.0 and CityBiz (all repeating the press release); CB Insights dates it 2024-02-07 and lists Neo only for the round. No competitor with a source dated near the 2020 batch was found; searches returned only 2024 and later pages. A single third party archive says Citron joined Gap in 2025; this is unverified and not used. The pre-2024 YC investment is not recorded because no amount was reported.
